subject: Home Management
preamble: The Home Management syllabus is designed to evaluate candidates' knowledge, appreciation, and application of fundamental management concepts, human and material resources, and decision-making processes essential for effective family living and societal contribution. It assesses practical skills in caring for the home, consumer education, nutrition, clothing, housing, health practices, and self-reliant entrepreneurial skills for daily life.
aims: Assess knowledge, understanding, appreciation, and application of management concepts, goals, values, standards, and needs;
Evaluate proficiency in applying decision-making and work-simplification processes in managing family resources;
Demonstrate effective utilization of human, material, and community resources available for home management;
Apply basic practical skills in caring for the home, managing family clothing, and maintaining personal and environmental health;
Develop critical consumer skills, awareness of consumer rights, and environmentally friendly consumption practices;
Promote sound health, safety, and sanitation practices within the home and immediate environment;
Cultivate self-reliant, creative, and entrepreneurial skills for wealth creation and effective living.
requirements: Candidates must take all three papers: Paper 1 (Objective), Paper 2 (Essay), and Paper 3 (Practical Test).
Paper 1 and Paper 2 are composite papers taken in a single sitting.
Paper 3 is a 3-hour practical examination conducted by an appointed visiting examiner.

examination_scheme.summary: The examination comprises three compulsory papers: Papers 1 and 2 are written composite tests, while Paper 3 evaluates practical home management skills.

papers.title: Objective Test
papers.details: Consists of fifty multiple-choice objective questions covering the entire syllabus. All questions are compulsory.

papers.title: Essay Test
papers.details: Consists of six essay questions. Candidates are required to answer any four questions.

papers.title: Practical Test
papers.details: A practical examination administered by a visiting examiner appointed by WAEC to assess practical proficiency in home management tasks.

topics.title: 1. Definition and Scope of Home Management
topics.notes: Definition, fundamental concepts, and potential career paths and opportunities related to Home Management.

topics.title: 2. The Management Process
topics.notes: Steps in management process: planning, organizing, implementing, and evaluating. Application of the process to specific home tasks.

topics.title: 3. Motivations for Home Management
topics.notes: Factors motivating management: personal characteristics, values, goals, standards, needs, and life events.

topics.title: 4. Family Resources and Work Simplification
topics.notes: Definition, characteristics, and classifications of resources: human (time, energy, skills) and non-human/material/community resources. Principles of work simplification applied to home activities.

topics.title: 5. Decision Making, Time, and Energy Management
topics.notes: Decision-making processes, steps in decision making, and techniques for efficient management of time and energy in the home.

topics.title: 1. The Family System
topics.notes: Definition and types of family (nuclear, monogamous, polygamous, extended); advantages and disadvantages of each. Stages of the family life cycle (beginning, expanding, contracting, empty-nest). Functions of the family, roles and responsibilities of members (parents, children, working mothers, single parents). Family relationships, factors influencing harmony, and conflict resolution mechanisms.

topics.title: 2. Courtship and Marriage
topics.notes: Types of marriage; interpersonal relationships (healthy guidelines, consequences of indiscriminate sexual behavior, sex education). Selecting a life partner (health factors: blood group, genotype, HIV status; dating, courtship, engagement). Preparation for marriage (maturity, financial readiness, family introductions). Traditional, religious, and civil marriage ceremonies.

topics.title: 3. Parenthood and Childcare
topics.notes: Preparation for parenthood: family planning, human reproduction, pregnancy, ante-natal care. Childbirth: labor, delivery, post-natal care, and immunization schedule. Parenting responsibilities: physical care, bathing, feeding, and meeting developmental needs.

topics.title: 1. Food Nutrients and Culinary Science
topics.notes: Classes of food nutrients, scientific study of functions and sources. Cooking terminology, basic cooking methods (moist, dry, combination), and the effect of heat on food nutrients.

topics.title: 2. Special Nutritional Needs and Meal Planning
topics.notes: Nutritional needs across life stages: infants, toddlers, adolescents, adults, pregnant/lactating women, the elderly, convalescents, invalids, and vegetarians. Principles of planning balanced meals for diverse groups.

topics.title: 3. Food Purchasing, Preservation, and Kitchen Management
topics.notes: Guidelines for economical and safe food purchasing. Methods and importance of food storage and preservation. Kitchen layout planning, hygiene practices, and safety measures.

topics.title: 4. Meal Service and Hospitality
topics.notes: Preparation and serving of meals, snacks, and beverages. Cooking equipment, utensils, tableware, table settings, and social etiquette in home entertaining.

topics.title: 1. Clothing and Textiles
topics.notes: Meaning, functions, and types of clothing. Classification and origin of textile fibers and fabrics. Fabric construction methods: weaving, knitting, crocheting, etc.

topics.title: 2. Household Linen and Wardrobe Planning
topics.notes: Types, selection, and functions of household linen. Guidelines for selecting, planning, and organizing wardrobes for individuals and families.

topics.title: 3. Care and Maintenance of Clothing
topics.notes: Laundry agents (water, soaps, detergents, fabric rinses, stiffening agents, bleaches) and equipment. Management of family wash, stain identification and removal techniques, care of special garments, sewing equipment, simple repairs, and proper storage techniques.

topics.title: 1. Choice and Acquisition of a Family House
topics.notes: Definition and types of houses (bungalow, duplex, storey building; traditional vs. modern). Methods of acquisition (renting, mortgage, building, buying, inheritance, gift). Economic, social, psychological, site, and ventilation factors influencing selection.

topics.title: 2. Setting Up a Home and Interior Decoration
topics.notes: Distinction between a house and a home. Equipment and furnishings (large/small equipment, hard/soft furnishings, fixtures). Elements and principles of design (color, texture, line, proportion, balance). Guidelines for interior decoration and flower arrangements.

topics.title: 3. Home Utilities, Maintenance, and Safety
topics.notes: Utilities: water sources, purification, and storage; electricity meter reading and billing; cooking fuels (gas, kerosene, firewood, charcoal, electricity). Cleaning agents, tools, and care of diverse surfaces (wood, tile, formica) and floor coverings (carpets, rugs, terrazzo, parquet). Functional area cleaning, bed making, safety measures, first aid, and prevention of home accidents.

topics.title: 4. Environmental Sanitation
topics.notes: Importance of environmental sanitation. Waste disposal methods (household waste, drainage systems, pollution prevention) and household pest control.

topics.title: 1. Creativity and Entrepreneurship
topics.notes: Meaning and importance of creativity and entrepreneurship. Entrepreneurial skills and small enterprise opportunities (fashion design, hair dressing, catering, bead making).

topics.title: 2. Money Management and Wealth Creation
topics.notes: Principles of money management; steps in family budgeting (income vs. expenditure). Meaning and methods of wealth creation (saving, trading, capital market investments: stocks, shares, treasury bills).

topics.title: 1. Consumer Rights, Responsibilities, and Information
topics.notes: Definition and importance of consumer education. Sources and uses of consumer information. Basic rights and responsibilities of consumers.

topics.title: 2. Legislation, Agencies, and Buying Practices
topics.notes: Consumer protection laws, regulatory agencies, and their functions. Wise purchasing practices, market survey procedures, and strategies for preventing home wastage through eco-friendly consumption.
